metadata.title: Derivative as Local Slope
metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.objective: Show a tangent line whose slope matches the derivative at a movable point.
metadata.learner: Can read coordinates on a graph.
misconceptions: Derivative is the value of the function
A positive derivative means the function is positive
expectedUnderstanding: The tangent slope equals the function's local slope
The sign of the rise matches the sign of the derivative
The derivative is separate from the function value

checkpoints.title: Negative slope
checkpoints.body: Set x to -2. The tangent falls to the right and the rise segment points downward, so the derivative is negative.

checkpoints.title: Zero slope
checkpoints.body: Set x to 0. The tangent is horizontal, the rise is zero, and f'(0) = 0 even though f(0) = -1.

checkpoints.title: Positive slope, negative value
checkpoints.body: Set x to 1.5. The tangent rises, so f'(1.5) = 0.75 is positive, while f(1.5) = -0.4375 is negative. The derivative is a slope, not a value.

narration.text: Move the point. The tangent and the small run-rise triangle share the same slope.
At the vertex the tangent is flat, so the derivative is zero.
On the right branch the tangent rises: positive slope, even though the function value is still negative.

fallback.text: The tangent at the moving point has slope f'(x) = 0.5x. The small rise-run triangle shows the same slope: when the rise is upward the derivative is positive, even if f(x) itself is negative.

accessibility.alt: A parabola with a movable point, a tangent line, and a small run-and-rise triangle. A vertical drop shows the function value; a slider moves the point from x = -3 to x = 3.
